applicabilityBasis.summary: dUSD is a dollar-referencing DeFi reserve-backed stablecoin marketed as a medium of on-chain credit and liquidity. Minting and redemption are permissionless smart-contract exchanges for eligible digital reserve assets, not a demonstrated obligation of an identified issuer to redeem for national currency or a bank deposit. Current terms disclaim guaranteed peg, legal redemption rights and fiduciary obligations while acknowledging multisignature and governance administration. The payment-stablecoin issuer/redemption elements of GENIUS therefore remain genuinely unresolved; a U.S. access restriction alone is not a statutory exclusion.

genius.notes: Current dUSD documentation describes chain-isolated reserves of other USD stablecoins, yieldcoins and Curve LP positions, with permissionless oracle-priced redemption into eligible reserve assets subject to liquidity and up to 0.5% fees. Public protocol reserve and redemption documentation is present; it is not a GENIUS-compliant reserve determination or a monthly independent fiat attestation. Current Terms of Use do not name a legal issuer or fiat redemption obligor and disclaim legal redemption rights, fiduciary duties and guarantees; they acknowledge multisignature, governance and contributor coordination over protocol-controlled systems. The primary introducing-dTRINITY article names Trinity Foundation Ltd. as the Singapore protocol developer. This establishes a project affiliation but does not settle whether the foundation is the statutory token issuer. Neither omission from current terms nor removal of a homepage attribution demonstrates that the foundation ceased or never held an issuer role. The pre-sweep issuerEntity is retained under the conservative adjudication rule because its deletion was not established at high confidence; this retention is not a new finding of GENIUS issuer status or fiat redemption liability. Issuer domicile remains unresolved; Cayman governing law is not proof of domicile. U.S., U.K. and Singapore are restricted under the protocol terms, but those restrictions do not independently establish GENIUS exclusion. No named public PPSI approval, section 5 application, state-qualified authorization or registered foreign exception was found in the prior dated negative-evidence review. The regime remains pre-effective on this review date; lack of authorization is not itself an assertion of present unlawful issuance.

negativeEvidenceReview.summary: No public GENIUS PPSI approval, official section 5 application, state-qualified authorization or registered foreign-issuer exception naming dTRINITY/dUSD or Trinity Foundation was located in the opened regulator sources and scoped exact-name searches as of 2026-10-07. The current protocol documentation and terms do not establish a legally identified fiat redemption obligor. Historical foundation corporate-directory assertions are not issuer authorization evidence; no global assertion that every relevant regulator was searched is made.
